findings: No retry/backoff/429 handling anywhere outside SignalR's reconnect loop: none of the 6 download-client actors (Qbit/Transmission/Deluge/Rtorrent/Sab/Nzbget) check for HTTP 429 or Retry-After; a single failed request just throws. Only qBittorrent and Deluge retry ONE time on a 401/403 session-expiry (re-login then retry), which is a distinct mechanism from rate-limit backoff.

SignalRConnection.runLoop is the only place with real backoff: exponential 1s->30s (doubling), and after 10 consecutive 'dead' cycles (no frame received AND under 30s minimumHealthyLifetime) it throttles to a 300s (5-minute) cold-start retry so a broken reverse-proxy can't pin the app at the 30s ceiling forever.

maxConcurrentSideLoads (=4, in ArrAPIClient.swift) and ParallelResolve (width 4-8, in DiscoverSources.swift / LocalToolBackend+Discover.swift) are unrelated to download clients or queue progress — they cap concurrent per-episode/per-album arr metadata side-loads and Discover/Quiz TMDB resolution fan-out respectively. Neither is used by QueueAggregator, RealtimeUpdates, or any download client.

Only 2 of 6 download clients have a real session/login concept: qBittorrent (SID cookie via /auth/login, or Bearer API key if username empty) and Deluge (auth.login cookie). Transmission uses a lightweight CSRF-style X-Transmission-Session-Id handshake (409 response header, retried once, not a login). rTorrent, SABnzbd, NZBGet have no session at all — Basic auth or apikey-in-query per request.

QueueAggregator caches one client instance per (kind, config) pair on itself (cachedQbitClient/cachedTransmissionClient/cachedDelugeClient only — NOT rTorrent/SABnzbd/NZBGet, which are constructed fresh on every performViaClient call) specifically to avoid re-login cost for the two clients that have a login handshake.

DownloadProgressService (not explicitly named in the task's file list but is the cache QueueAggregator calls into) is the single point fronting all 6 clients' fetchProgress(ids:): 2s TTL to coalesce bursty poll+realtime refreshes into one round-trip, 60s maxCacheAge before falling back to arr-reported progress, and a 'some clients failed vs all clients failed' distinction so a transient blip doesn't snap progress bars back to stale arr values.

RealtimeFrameParsingTests.swift (11 @Test cases) covers ONLY the pure SignalRConnection.parse(frame:source:) function — envelope shape, name-casing, queueStatus resource extraction, malformed/close/ping frames, missing-arguments fallback. It does NOT test negotiate(), the WebSocket handshake consumeHandshake(), the backoff/reconnect loop in runLoop(), or ping pump timing — those paths are untested at the unit level.

Widget target dependency check: ArrBarrWidgets.swift only calls WidgetDataStore (serviceConfig/isDemoActive) plus LibrarySummaryService/UpcomingService (both build arr clients directly). None of the 6 download clients, QueueAggregator, RealtimeUpdates, ConnectionHealthMonitor, or DownloadProgressService are referenced anywhere under ArrBarrWidgets/ — the widget never touches download-client/realtime code at all, confirming that whole subsystem is queue-popover-only.

ConnectionHealth.swift + ConnectionHealthState.swift + ServerStatusModel.swift + ServerStatusView.swift are UI/state-composition layers that CONSUME probe/health results (from ConnectionHealthMonitor and QueueViewModel) but issue no network calls of their own except ServerStatusModel's own /diskspace fetch (which goes to the arrs, not download clients) — correctly classified as staying in ArrCore, not moving to MediaKit.

systemDidWake() (QueueViewModel) does exactly two things: realtime.forceReconnect() (tear down + rebuild every SignalR socket immediately, bypassing the reconnect loop's backoff) then refresh() (full 4-arr + progress poll) — this is the only wake-specific code path in scope; there is no separate wake handling inside RealtimeUpdates.swift itself beyond forceReconnect() being called.

The task asks for 'coalescing window for SignalR bursts' — QueueViewModel.realtimeBurstWindow (0.25s) plus realtimeRefreshFloor() (1s popover-open / backgroundInterval popover-closed) is the coalescing logic, but it lives in QueueViewModel (view-model/domain layer), not in RealtimeUpdates.swift itself. RealtimeUpdates.swift only exposes raw per-event dispatch with no batching of its own — confirm this split (transport emits raw events; view-model coalesces) is the intended MediaKit boundary, i.e. whether the coalescing logic itself is meant to move into MediaKit's communication layer or stay in ArrCore's QueueViewModel.

ArrMCPServer package also depends on ArrCore's download-client types indirectly (ToolCatalogBridge/LocalToolBackend can trigger queue pause/resume/delete via QueueAggregator) — not explored in this pass since it was out of the given scope; worth a follow-up inventory if MediaKit's client swap needs to keep the MCP tool surface working.
summary: Full inventory of ArrBarr's download-client / progress / realtime / health subsystem (ArrCore, scope: download clients, progress, realtime, health), gathered read-only against branch feat/mediakit-foundation. Six download-client actors (QbittorrentClient, TransmissionClient, DelugeClient, RtorrentClient, SabnzbdClient, NzbgetClient — 1412 LOC combined) each conform to two shared protocols (DownloadProgressSource in Models/DownloadProgress.swift, DownloadAddSource in Models/DownloadDrop.swift; no 'protocol DownloadClient' exists under that name). QueueAggregator.swift (695 LOC) merges the 4 arrs' queues with download-client progress fetched through DownloadProgressService.swift (141 LOC, 2s TTL / 60s max-staleness cache), matched by lowercased downloadId, and routes pause/resume/delete/continue actions to whichever client's user-chosen name best matches. RealtimeUpdates.swift (751 LOC) is a hand-rolled SignalR-over-WebSocket client (no third-party SDK) with per-arr negotiate/handshake/backoff, tested only at the frame-parsing level by RealtimeFrameParsingTests.swift (11 cases, transport/backoff untested). ConnectionHealthMonitor.swift (115 LOC) probes all 6 download clients + OpenAI/TMDB/media-server testConnection() once per 60s. All ten of these files are candidates for replaced_by_mediakit=true (3113 LOC total); QueueViewModel, ConnectionHealth, ServerStatusModel/View, ConnectionHealthState, WidgetDataStore, LibrarySummaryService and UpcomingService stay in ArrCore as domain/view-model/widget composition. The WidgetKit target never touches any download-client or realtime code directly. No 429/Retry-After handling exists anywhere outside SignalR's own exponential-backoff reconnect loop.
